subject: Post-demo recap + integration proposal (SDK auth, routing & model fallback plan)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@zephyrhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@zephyrhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 19:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick demo follow-up

Thanks for the demo earlier — Hannah. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we loop infra: 1) We run most inference from a US primary region but have EU fallbacks for GDPR-sensitive patients; can Redwood route by region automatically? 2) On auth: we prefer mutual TLS + short-lived tokens for internal services (not simple static keys). 3) Embeddings: we'd like to know recommended vector dimensions and index approach for our existing clinical QA index (~2M documents).

Happy to have Samir and our infra engineer join a technical sync if useful.

- Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
ZephyrHealth
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@zephyrhealth.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 20:03:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed PoC approach

Elena — great to meet you both. Quick recap and concrete recommendations so Zephyr can validate in a 4-week PoC: 

1) Region routing: Redwood can do policy-based routing at request time. Proposal: default to us-east for latency-sensitive calls, and route by data-class tag when request includes 'gdpr:eu' to eu-west (automatic region binding). We will include a routing policy in the PoC that demonstrates automatic region shift and cross-region fallbacks.

2) Auth model: we support mTLS and short-lived workload tokens (via your KMS/OIDC provider). For the PoC we will: provide an mTLS sample config and an SDK sample that exchanges a short-lived token through your auth gateway. No static API keys required. Dev will provide the sample.

3) SDK & structured output/tool-calling: Our SDK supports structured output annotations and tool calling hooks. For clinical QA, we recommend enforcing response schemas for PHI-sanitized outputs and using tool calls for deterministic lookups (patient-lookup microservice). We'll include a quickstart PDF with the SDK flow.

4) Embeddings & reranker: For a ~2M doc index we recommend 1024-d embeddings, product-quantized indexes (PQ8) for cost/space tradeoffs, and a small neural reranker (distil) for top-100 candidate rerank to improve precision. We'll provide estimated storage and token-costs in the MAP.

5) Model routing & fallback policy: propose primary = rdx-compat/gptx-8b-quant (fast, low-cost), fallback #1 = rdx-compat/gptx-13b-quant (higher quality), fallback #2 = hosted gptx-13b-ptx for peak latency-tolerant queries. Policies will evaluate latency SLA (p95), per-request cost budget, and an optional 'quality_margin' flag set per endpoint.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf, zephyr_proof_of_concept_map.xlsx (high-level MAP + timeline).

Next steps (proposed):
- Technical sync (1 hr) with Dev + your infra engineer — schedule this week?
- We’ll turn the PoC MAP into a runnable config in our sandbox account with sample routing policies.
- Zephyr provides a short list of 3 representative prompt+eval examples (sensitivity & desired output schema).

If that all sounds good I’ll loop in Dylan on the routing policy config and have Dev produce the mTLS + token exchange sample.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Zephyr PoC: ask for SDK auth sample + routing policy draft

Dev / Dylan — copying summary of the Zephyr demo and their asks (Elena + Samir). Please see two quick engineering asks below: 

A) Dev: please produce an mTLS + short-lived token example. Keep it as: 1) sample server cert instructions; 2) token exchange snippet using OIDC on behalf of client; 3) SDK sample call which attaches both mTLS and token. Target: simple Node/Go example, separate sections for private and hosted deployments. Attach to reply and add a short README.

B) Dylan: we need a routing policy draft that implements: region override tag ('gdpr:eu'), latency-first path (p95 < 120ms) for 'interactive' endpoints, cost-cap for batch endpoints (per-token budget), and a fallback chain preference order I listed. Represent policy as plain English and a pseudo-config YAML sample.

Timeline: can we get both by EOD tomorrow (Wed 7/7)? Zephyr wants a technical sync this week; I told them Wed/Thu windows.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@zephyrhealth.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@zephyrhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Zephyr PoC: ask for SDK auth sample + routing policy draft

Hannah / Dylan / Elena / Samir — pulling together the code samples now. Quick technical notes so the sync can be productive: 

- mTLS + token flow: I'll provide a Node example that uses client certs for the TLS handshake and then exchanges an OIDC assertion for a short-lived Redwood workload token via the token_introspect endpoint. The SDK will accept both the client certificate path and a token in its config (we'll show how to do this in the Quickstart PDF).

- Routing policy draft: Dylan and I discussed a simple JSON policy schema I'll include. Key hooks: request.metadata.region_hint, request.metadata.privacy_class, request.metadata.interactive (bool). Policy engine will evaluate (1) explicit region_hint, (2) privacy_class (force eu-west), (3) latency target, (4) cost budget. Fallback ordering is enforced by policy weights.

- Embeddings: I ran a quick cost estimate for 2M docs at 1024-d with PQ8: ~6 TB raw, ~700GB PQ storage, and a ~30% cost reduction vs dense 2048. I'll attach a short spreadsheet with estimates (in the MAP). For reranker we recommend a distil-bert-based scorer for top-100.

I will attach the Node sample, policy draft (pseudo-YAML), and updated MAP to the shared Drive link before the sync. Confirming a slot: Wed 7/7 11:00 AM ET works for me.

- Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
